Explanation: ':has()' is CSS's long-awaited parent/relational selector. 'article:has(img)' targets the

element itself if it contains an .

Question 22: What is the difference between ':is()' and ':where()' in modern CSS?

2 Points
A) ':is()' has zero specificity; ':where()' takes the highest specificity
B) ':is()' takes the specificity of its most specific selector argument; ':where()' always has ZERO specificity (0, 0, 0, 0) ✓ Correct
C) ':where()' only works on input elements
D) There is no difference
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) ':is()' takes the specificity of its most specific selector argument; ':where()' always has ZERO specificity (0, 0, 0, 0)

Explanation: Both reduce selector duplication, but ':where()' always has 0 specificity, making it ideal for CSS reset and default utility rules that are easy to override.

Question 23: What does 'animation-fill-mode: forwards' specify?

2 Points
A) The animation plays forward and then in reverse
B) The target element retains the computed style values from the last keyframe after the animation finishes ✓ Correct
C) The animation repeats forever
D) The animation applies styles before starting
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) The target element retains the computed style values from the last keyframe after the animation finishes

Explanation: 'animation-fill-mode: forwards' causes the element to retain the styling defined in the final keyframe (100% or 'to') after the animation ends.

Question 24: Which CSS property enables GPU hardware acceleration for smooth 60fps animations?

2 Points
A) gpu: enable;
B) transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0); or will-change: transform; ✓ Correct
C) accelerate: true;
D) render-mode: hardware;
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0); or will-change: transform;

Explanation: Applying 3D transforms (translate3d/translateZ) or 'will-change: transform' promotes the element to its own GPU compositor layer, bypassing expensive main-thread CPU repaints.

Question 25: What is the CSS 'gap' property used for?

2 Points
A) Sets the margin around the body element
B) Defines the gutter spacing between rows and columns in Flexbox and CSS Grid containers without adding outer margins ✓ Correct
C) Controls letter spacing in text
D) Inserts a blank paragraph
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Defines the gutter spacing between rows and columns in Flexbox and CSS Grid containers without adding outer margins

Explanation: 'gap' (and row-gap/column-gap) sets gutters between children in CSS Grid and modern Flexbox without needing negative margins on wrappers.

Question 26: What does the 'contain: strict' or 'contain: content' property do in CSS?

2 Points
A) Locks the aspect ratio of images
B) Tells the browser engine that the element's subtree is completely isolated from the rest of the DOM, enabling massive layout/paint performance optimizations ✓ Correct
C) Prevents text selection
D) Centers content horizontally
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Tells the browser engine that the element's subtree is completely isolated from the rest of the DOM, enabling massive layout/paint performance optimizations

Explanation: CSS Containment (contain: layout paint size) isolates an element's rendering subtree, so the browser doesn't have to recompute the entire page layout on internal DOM mutations.

Question 27: What is the difference between 'opacity: 0' and 'pointer-events: none'?

2 Points
A) No difference
B) 'opacity: 0' makes the element visually transparent but it still receives mouse clicks and blocks underlying elements; 'pointer-events: none' allows clicks to pass straight through the element to layers underneath ✓ Correct
C) 'pointer-events: none' makes text bold
D) 'opacity: 0' removes the element from the DOM
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) 'opacity: 0' makes the element visually transparent but it still receives mouse clicks and blocks underlying elements; 'pointer-events: none' allows clicks to pass straight through the element to layers underneath

Explanation: 'opacity: 0' elements still intercept mouse events and block clicks to layers below. 'pointer-events: none' disables click and hover interception, letting events pass through.

Question 28: What does the 'backdrop-filter: blur(10px)' property do?

2 Points
A) Blurs the foreground text of the element
B) Applies a graphical blur effect to the area BEHIND the element (essential for frosted-glass glassmorphism design) ✓ Correct
C) Blurs the browser background wallpaper
D) Applies a drop shadow
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Applies a graphical blur effect to the area BEHIND the element (essential for frosted-glass glassmorphism design)

Explanation: Unlike 'filter: blur()', which blurs the element itself, 'backdrop-filter: blur()' filters the pixels rendered directly behind a semi-transparent element, creating frosted glass.

Question 29: Which CSS property is used to truncate overflow text with an ellipsis (...)?

2 Points
A) text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; ✓ Correct
B) overflow: ellipsis;
C) text-truncate: true;
D) text-wrap: none;
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (A) text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden;

Explanation: Single-line text truncation requires the triumvirate: 'overflow: hidden', 'white-space: nowrap', and 'text-overflow: ellipsis'.

Question 30: What does the 'aspect-ratio' property achieve in modern CSS?

2 Points 
img { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; width: 100%; }
A) Sets the focal length of responsive cameras
B) Enforces a defined width-to-height ratio on an element without requiring padding-top layout hacks ✓ Correct
C) Rotates the image 16 degrees
D) Sets viewport zoom
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Enforces a defined width-to-height ratio on an element without requiring padding-top layout hacks

Explanation: The 'aspect-ratio: 16 / 9' property allows browsers to automatically calculate the element's height based on its width, reserving layout space and preventing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).

sharing the same parent

Explanation: The '+' combinator selects the element immediately preceded by the former element with the same parent. (The general sibling combinator '~' selects all subsequent siblings).

A) Only the first

elements that follow

Explanation: The general sibling combinator '~' matches all sibling elements that occur anywhere after the reference element under the same parent.

Question 33: What does 'transform-origin' control?

2 Points
A) The location of the original file
B) The point of origin around which transforms (rotation, scaling, skewing) are calculated (default is 50% 50% 0) ✓ Correct
C) The CSS animation start time
D) The z-index layer coordinate
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) The point of origin around which transforms (rotation, scaling, skewing) are calculated (default is 50% 50% 0)

Explanation: 'transform-origin' sets the pivot point for geometric transformations. By default, it is centered at '50% 50%' (the center of the element's bounding box).

Question 34: What is the difference between 'currentColor' and standard color keywords in CSS?

2 Points
A) 'currentColor' is an invalid CSS value
B) 'currentColor' is a CSS keyword that takes the computed value of the element's current 'color' property, enabling dynamic SVG icon fills and borders ✓ Correct
C) 'currentColor' reflects the OS theme color
D) 'currentColor' only works on hyperlinks
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) 'currentColor' is a CSS keyword that takes the computed value of the element's current 'color' property, enabling dynamic SVG icon fills and borders

Explanation: 'currentColor' dynamically inherits the value of the CSS 'color' property, allowing SVG fills, borders, and shadows to automatically adapt to text color changes.

Question 35: What does the 'overscroll-behavior: contain' property prevent?

2 Points
A) Prevents scrollbars from appearing
B) Prevents scroll chaining and browser bounce/pull-to-refresh when reaching scroll boundaries inside a modal or drawer ✓ Correct
C) Smooth scrolling
D) Horizontal overflow
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Prevents scroll chaining and browser bounce/pull-to-refresh when reaching scroll boundaries inside a modal or drawer

Explanation: 'overscroll-behavior: contain' prevents scrolling from propagating to parent containers (scroll chaining) when the inner container reaches its boundary.

Question 36: Which pseudo-class applies styles when an element is focused specifically via keyboard navigation (e.g. Tab key) rather than a mouse click?

A) :focus
B) :focus-visible ✓ Correct
C) :focus-within
D) :active
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) :focus-visible

Explanation: ':focus-visible' only activates when the user interacts using a non-pointing device (like a keyboard), keeping visual focus rings for accessibility while removing them for mouse clicks.

Question 37: What does the ':focus-within' pseudo-class match?

2 Points 
form:focus-within { border-color: blue; }
A) The form itself if it has autofocus
B) The container element if the element itself OR ANY of its descendants has focus ✓ Correct
C) The first input of the form
D) Disabled form inputs
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) The container element if the element itself OR ANY of its descendants has focus

Explanation: ':focus-within' targets a parent element if any of its children currently possess focus (e.g., highlighting an entire form card when typing inside an input).

Question 38: How does the 'calc()' CSS function handle operator spacing?

2 Points

B) Spaces are mandatory around addition (+) and subtraction (-) operators to differentiate them from negative numbers ✓ Correct
C) Spaces are only allowed around division
D) calc() only accepts pixel units
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Spaces are mandatory around addition (+) and subtraction (-) operators to differentiate them from negative numbers

Explanation: In calc(), the '+' and '-' operators MUST have whitespace on both sides (e.g. '100% - 20px', not '100%-20px') because a minus without spaces is parsed as a negative sign.

Question 39: What is the CSS cascade hierarchy order from lowest to highest priority?

A) User styles -> Browser default (User Agent) -> Author styles
B) Browser default (User Agent) -> User normal styles -> Author normal styles -> Author !important -> User !important ✓ Correct
C) Inline styles -> ID -> Class -> Tag
D) Author styles always override !important

Answer: (B) Browser default (User Agent) -> User normal styles -> Author normal styles -> Author !important -> User !important

Explanation: The CSS Cascade evaluates origins: Browser defaults (User Agent) are lowest, followed by User normal styles, Author normal styles, Author !important, and finally User !important as highest.

Answer: (B) Explicitly controls the cascade precedence and specificity order between different stylesheets (e.g. ensuring component styles always override third-party framework styles)

Explanation: Cascade Layers (@layer) give developers explicit control over the cascade order regardless of selector specificity, resolving third-party CSS specificity wars.

Question 41: What does the 'line-height: 1.5' unitless number mean?

B) Multiplies the element's computed font-size by 1.5 to determine line box height without inheriting fixed pixel values to children ✓ Correct

D) Sets line spacing to 150%
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Multiplies the element's computed font-size by 1.5 to determine line box height without inheriting fixed pixel values to children

Explanation: A unitless line-height (e.g. 1.5) scales proportionally with the font-size of each descendant element, preventing overlapping text that happens with inherited fixed units.

Question 42: What does the 'isolation: isolate' property accomplish?

2 Points
A) Isolates the element in an iframe
B) Creates a new Stacking Context without needing to set opacity, transform, or z-index ✓ Correct
C) Prevents CSS variables from inheriting
D) Disconnects the element from the DOM
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Creates a new Stacking Context without needing to set opacity, transform, or z-index

Explanation: 'isolation: isolate' creates a new stacking context on the element cleanly, preventing child z-indexes and mix-blend-modes from bleeding into outer siblings.

Question 43: What is the difference between 'filter: drop-shadow()' and 'box-shadow'?

B) 'box-shadow' draws a rectangular shadow conforming to the element's box model; 'filter: drop-shadow()' conforms to the actual transparent contours and alpha channel of PNG/SVG shapes ✓ Correct

💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) 'box-shadow' draws a rectangular shadow conforming to the element's box model; 'filter: drop-shadow()' conforms to the actual transparent contours and alpha channel of PNG/SVG shapes

Explanation: 'box-shadow' creates a shadow around the rectangular box. 'filter: drop-shadow()' traces the transparent alpha channel of PNG images and SVGs, casting shadows around the actual artwork.

Question 44: What does the 'ch' unit represent in CSS?

A) 1 centimeter
B) The advance width of the character '0' (zero) in the element's current font (ideal for limiting line lengths in reading typography) ✓ Correct
C) Character height
D) 1 channel in RGB
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) The advance width of the character '0' (zero) in the element's current font (ideal for limiting line lengths in reading typography)

Explanation: The 'ch' unit equals the width of the character '0' in the current font. Setting 'max-width: 65ch' is the gold standard for comfortable reading typography (45-75 chars/line).

Question 45: What does the 'font-display: swap' descriptor do in an '@font-face' rule?

B) Instructs the browser to render text immediately using a fallback system font, swapping to the custom web font as soon as it downloads (eliminating Flash of Invisible Text - FOIT) ✓ Correct
C) Swaps font weights dynamically
D) Disables web fonts on slow connections
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Instructs the browser to render text immediately using a fallback system font, swapping to the custom web font as soon as it downloads (eliminating Flash of Invisible Text - FOIT)

Explanation: 'font-display: swap' eliminates FOIT (Flash of Invisible Text) by using a fallback font during download, then instantly swapping to the custom font once loaded.

Question 46: What does 'scrollbar-gutter: stable' do in modern CSS?

A) Customizes the scrollbar thumb color
B) Reserves space for the scrollbar beforehand, preventing jarring layout shifts when scrollable content appears and disappears ✓ Correct
C) Hides the scrollbar completely
D) Makes the scrollbar thicker
💡 View Answer & Explanation

Answer: (B) Reserves space for the scrollbar beforehand, preventing jarring layout shifts when scrollable content appears and disappears

Explanation: 'scrollbar-gutter: stable' reserves layout space for the scrollbar gutter, preventing content jumping horizontally when scrollbars toggle on dynamic page heights.

A) Form inputs that contain no value
B) Elements that have no child nodes at all (including text nodes and whitespace) ✓ Correct

D) Unstyled div containers

Answer: (B) Elements that have no child nodes at all (including text nodes and whitespace)

Explanation: ':empty' matches elements that have zero child elements and zero text nodes (even whitespace counts as a child text node unless using modern ':blank').

Question 49: What does the 'pointer-events: none' property do when applied to an element?

2 Points
A) Changes the cursor to a pointer
B) Prevents the element from receiving mouse/touch events (clicks, hovers), allowing events to pass through to underlying elements ✓ Correct

CSS Interview Questions & Answers

Interview Preparation ⏱️ 20 min read

Curated technical interview questions covering foundational principles, edge cases, and high-level architectural patterns frequently encountered in CSS developer interviews.

Q1: Explain the CSS Box Model.

Easy
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
Every HTML element rendered in a document is treated as a rectangular box comprising four concentric layers:
  • Content: The actual text, image, or media of the element.
  • Padding: Transparent spacing between content and the border.
  • Border: A line surrounding the padding and content.
  • Margin: Transparent spacing outside the border separating this element from adjacent elements.
Using box-sizing: border-box is standard practice in modern CSS so specified widths encompass content, padding, and border.

Q2: What is CSS Specificity and how is it calculated?

Medium
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
Specificity determines which CSS rule applies to an element when multiple conflicting rules target it. It is computed as a 4-part tuple (Inline, ID, Class/Attribute/Pseudo-class, Element/Pseudo-element):
  • Inline styles: (1, 0, 0, 0) e.g., style='color:red'
  • IDs: (0, 1, 0, 0) e.g., #header
  • Classes, attributes, pseudo-classes: (0, 0, 1, 0) e.g., .btn, [type='text'], :hover
  • Elements, pseudo-elements: (0, 0, 0, 1) e.g., div, ::before
!important overrides normal specificity, but should be avoided to prevent specificity wars.

Q3: What is the difference between Flexbox and CSS Grid?

Medium
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
Core Distinctions:
  • Flexbox: One-Dimensional: Optimized for laying out elements in a single dimension (either row OR column at a time). Ideal for navbars, toolbars, and dynamic content-driven spacing.
  • CSS Grid: Two-Dimensional: Optimized for laying out rows AND columns simultaneously. Ideal for complex whole-page layouts, dashboard grids, and template layouts where precise column and row alignment is needed.

Q4: What is a Stacking Context and why does z-index sometimes not work?

Hard
📖 View Technical Answer & Deep-Dive
A stacking context is a three-dimensional conceptualization of HTML elements along an imaginary z-axis relative to the screen. z-index only works on positioned elements (position other than static) or flex/grid children.

Common reasons z-index fails:
  • The element has position: static (default).
  • A parent element formed a new stacking context (via opacity < 1, transform, filter, or clip-path), constraining children within the parent's z-index level regardless of high child z-index values.
